paraphrase: He reviews this body from the soles up and the hair down, bounded by skin, full of many kinds of impurity — head hair, body hair … urine — as a man with eyes would review a double-mouthed bag of mixed grains.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: He reviews this body however placed as consisting of elements — earth, water, fire and air — as a skilled butcher who has slaughtered a cow sits at a crossroads with it cut into pieces.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: As if seeing a corpse in a charnel ground — one, two or three days dead, bloated and festering; devoured by crows, vultures, dogs and worms; a skeleton with flesh and blood held by sinews; without flesh; bones scattered; bones bleached white; heaped up; crumbled to dust — he compares his own body with it: 'this body too is of the same nature, will be like that, is not exempt from that fate' (the nine charnel-ground contemplations).
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: This is the direct path (ekāyana) for the purification of beings, for surmounting sorrow and lamentation, for the passing away of pain and grief, for attaining the method, for realising nibbāna: the four establishments of mindfulness.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked). 'Ekāyana' is rendered 'the only way' by some and 'the direct path' / 'path to convergence' by others; the commentary gives several senses.

original.text: “Ekāyano ayaṁ, bhikkhave, maggo sattānaṁ visuddhiyā, sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya, dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya, ñāyassa adhigamāya, nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṁ cattāro satipaṭṭhānā.
original.script: Roman (Pali; SuttaCentral/Mahāsaṅgīti romanization with ṁ for niggahīta)

paraphrase: A monk abides contemplating the body in the body, feelings in feelings, mind in mind, dhammas in dhammas — ardent, clearly comprehending and mindful, having removed covetousness and grief for the world.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

original.text: Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ; vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ; citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ; dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
original.script: Roman (Pali; SuttaCentral/Mahāsaṅgīti romanization with ṁ for niggahīta)

paraphrase: Contemplating feelings: feeling a pleasant, painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling he knows it as such, and knows each as worldly (of the flesh) or unworldly.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: Contemplating mind: he knows the mind with lust as with lust, without lust as without lust; with and without hatred and delusion; contracted and scattered; exalted and unexalted; surpassable and unsurpassable; concentrated and unconcentrated; liberated and unliberated.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: Contemplating dhammas as the five hindrances: when sensual desire is present he knows it is present; when absent he knows it is absent; he knows how the unarisen arises, how the arisen is abandoned, and how the abandoned does not arise again in future — and likewise for ill will, dullness and drowsiness, restlessness and remorse, and doubt.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: Contemplating dhammas as the five aggregates of clinging: 'such is form, such its arising, such its passing away' — and so for feeling, perception, formations and consciousness.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: Gone to the forest, the root of a tree or an empty hut, sitting cross-legged, body erect, mindfulness established, he breathes in and out mindfully, knowing long and short breaths and training to experience the whole body and to calm the bodily formation, like a skilled turner knowing a long or short turn.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: Contemplating dhammas as the six internal and external sense bases: he knows the eye, forms and the fetter that arises dependent on both, how the unarisen fetter arises, how the arisen is abandoned and how the abandoned does not arise again.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: Contemplating dhammas as the seven factors of awakening: he knows each factor as present or absent, how the unarisen arises and how the arisen comes to fulfilment by development.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: Contemplating dhammas as the four noble truths: he knows as it really is 'this is suffering', 'this is its origin', 'this is its cessation', 'this is the way'.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: Whoever develops the four establishments of mindfulness in this way for seven years — or even for seven days — may expect one of two fruits: final knowledge here and now or, if there is a residue, non-return.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: The refrain: he abides contemplating the body internally, externally and both; contemplating its nature of arising, of passing away, and of both; or mindfulness that 'there is a body' is simply established to the extent needed for knowledge and mindfulness; he abides independent, not clinging to anything in the world.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

original.text: Iti ajjhattaṁ vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati, bahiddhā vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā vā kāye kāyānupassī viharati; samudayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṁ viharati, vayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṁ viharati, samudayavayadhammānupassī vā kāyasmiṁ viharati. ‘Atthi kāyo’ti vā panassa sati paccupaṭṭhitā hoti. Yāvadeva ñāṇamattāya paṭissatimattāya anissito ca viharati, na ca kiñci loke upādiyati.

paraphrase: He knows 'I am walking', 'standing', 'sitting', 'lying down' however the body is disposed; and he acts with clear comprehension in going and returning, looking ahead and aside, bending and stretching, wearing robes, eating and drinking, defecating, walking, standing, sitting, falling asleep, waking, talking and keeping silent.
